title: A dynamic brain for MIRROR's live interview practice
decision: Build a multi-agent orchestration system for live interview practice, or something simpler?

options.label: Full multi-agent orchestration, live every turn
One interviewer LLM with structured state
Hybrid: deterministic orchestrator + one fast LLM call, analysts off the live path
Keep sequential, fix repeats with a tagged bank and asked-history

graham.reason: Do testers get a better practice session, and does it show in what they do next

musk.reason: What is the real constraint, and what is the simplest thing that removes it

bezos.reason: Is it a one-way door, and does it work backwards from the candidate's experience

buffett.reason: Downside: latency, cost, failure modes and the no-scores trust promise

brief: MIRROR's live interview questions repeat because a fixed four-line script is the fallback and nothing remembers what was asked. The founder leans toward a multi-agent orchestration system. Options A to D range from full agents to a minimal fix.
assumptions: A handful of testers, no revenue (assumed)
About two weeks to beta invites (assumed)
Free-tier hosted model with rate limits (assumed)
